fullPassage:
My Octopus Teacher

I returned to the Cape of Good Hope, South Africa, where I had spent my childhood, after over 20 years of movie-making. I went diving in the cold sea off the coast of the Cape, and it was among the dense seaweed forests where I met an octopus.

First Encounter

I saw a fish peacefully swimming near a heap of shells. Suddenly, an octopus sprang from the heap and grabbed the fish. Amazed at the cleverness of the octopus, I swam a little closer, but it disappeared. In fact, it had lifted a piece of seaweed, wrapped it around itself, and was staring at me out of a little gap. What an extraordinary creature! I wondered what would happen if I kept watching it. To see the world from the octopus's perspective, I left a camera near the den and started visiting regularly. I even mapped the environment around the den. Expecting some drama to come, I waited.

Making Friends

The octopus became less scared as I visited more often. After about a month, it came near me. I put my hand out, and it reached out to me. After another week, it started to wave like a human friend saying, "Hi, I'm excited to see you." I kept still, and it covered my whole hand. Since I had to take a breath, I swam toward the surface. To my surprise, it rode on my hand all the way to the top. There I was, just staring into the eyes of this incredible creature. It sparked my curiosity in a way that I had not experienced before. Had I gained its trust? I started reading books about octopuses, but I wanted to learn more about this marvelous creature. The first thing I learned was that "it" was a "she."

Getting Closer

Danger in the form of pyjama sharks, the area's biggest predators, came with little warning in the sea. The octopus was moving around near the edge of the seaweed forest, and I saw a shark tracking her. In an instant, she swam into a crack to escape, but the shark was faster.

The shark had taken a bite of one of her arms and was waiting for her. I wanted to save my friend, but in this environment, I could only observe. She managed to get deeper into the crack, but she was bleeding. After a while, the shark lost interest, and the octopus used the opportunity to get back to her den, without one of her arms. She was in serious danger because her arms function like the hands, legs, nose, and eyes of humans.

The next day, I was relieved to see that she had survived. She was weak, and her colors were not as bright. I checked on her every day, wondering if that day would be the last. It was emotionally painful to witness these things happening to her.

Recovery, Growth, and Sacrifice

A short while later, I saw that the wound had healed. To my amazement, a little arm started to grow back, and she started to become active again. I started to compare my life to life in the unforgiving sea. I thought of what was valuable in life. I began to spend more time with my family and friends, and I even started to dive with my young son. He became just as interested in her as I was. As the octopus's arm became more functional, I felt things in my life were improving too.

An octopus's average life is about a year, which ends after reproducing. One day, eight months after meeting her, I found her with another octopus. It was bittersweet knowing her final days were approaching even though she would bear young.

After mating, she didn't come out of her den. There would be no feeding or hunting. She was timing her final moments for the hatching of her eggs. After the eggs hatched, she died. A few months later, my son found a little octopus. We believe her story continues on.

I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing wildness she represented. I built a relationship with her and witnessed her life up to the final moments. I saw her from a perspective that I could not have had without this experience. She was smart, sensitive, and strong, often going through rough and tough days just like humans do. Eventually, she committed herself to protecting the birth of her young before she died. As a human being, I found something noble in that sacrifice. She was not simply an octopus; she was a part of this world just as I am a part of it now, and in that sense, we all have our own stories to tell.

questions.passage: I saw a fish peacefully swimming near a heap of shells. Suddenly, an octopus sprang from the heap and ①<u>grabbed</u> the fish. ②<u>Amazing</u> at the cleverness of the octopus, I swam a little closer, but it ③<u>disappeared</u>. In fact, it had lifted a piece of seaweed, wrapped it around ④<u>itself</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 문어의 영리함에 놀란(Amazed) 나는. Amazing → Amazed (감정을 느끼는 주어 → 과거분사)
det.analysis:
✅ ② Amazing → Amazed: 주어 I가 놀라움을 '느끼는' 대상이므로 과거분사(Amazed) 사용
❌ ① grabbed(잡았다): 과거형 정상
❌ ③ disappeared(사라졌다): 과거형 정상
❌ ④ itself(그 자신): 재귀대명사 (it → itself) 정상
det.tip: 감정 분사: -ed(감정을 느끼는 사람) vs -ing(감정을 유발하는 대상). I am amazed / It is amazing

questions.passage: It sparked my curiosity in a way that I had not ①<u>experienced</u> before. Had I ②<u>gained</u> its trust? I started reading books about octopuses, but I wanted to learn more about this marvelous creature. The first thing I ③<u>learning</u> was that 'it' was ④<u>a</u> 'she.'
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 내가 배운(learned) 첫 번째 것은. learning → learned (과거형 서술어)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ learning → learned: The first thing I learned was ~. 주절의 서술어이므로 과거형 필요
❌ ① experienced: had + p.p.(과거완료) 정상
❌ ② gained: Had I gained (과거완료 의문문) 정상
❌ ④ a: 관사 a + she(명사화) 정상
det.tip: The first thing I learned was ~ = 내가 배운 첫 번째 것은. learned = 과거형 서술어, learning은 불가

questions.passage: I checked on her every day, ①<u>wondering</u> if that day would be the last. It was emotionally painful to ②<u>witness</u> these things happening to her. A short while later, I saw that the wound had ③<u>healed</u>. To my amazement, a little arm started to grow back, and she started to become ④<u>actively</u> again.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 다시 활동적이(active) 되기 시작했다. actively → active (become + 형용사 보어)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ actively → active: become은 보어로 형용사를 취함. 부사 actively는 불가
❌ ① wondering(궁금해하며): 분사구문 정상
❌ ② witness(목격하다): to부정사 (painful to witness) 정상
❌ ③ healed(치유되었다): had + p.p.(과거완료) 정상
det.tip: become + 형용사(보어): become active(활동적이 되다). 부사 actively는 보어 불가

questions.passage: The octopus became less ①<u>scared</u> as I visited more often. After about a month, it came near me. I put my hand out, and it ②<u>reached</u> out to me. After another week, it started to wave like a human friend. I kept ③<u>still</u>, and it covered my whole hand. Since I had to take a breath, I swam toward the ④<u>bottom</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 숨을 쉬어야 했으므로 수면(surface)을 향해 헤엄쳤다. bottom(바닥)은 surface(수면)의 반의어이므로 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ bottom(바닥) → surface(수면)가 원문. 숨을 쉬려면 수면으로 올라가야 함. bottom은 반대
❌ ① scared(겁먹은): 원문 그대로
❌ ② reached(뻗었다): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ still(가만히): 원문 그대로
det.tip: surface(수면) ↔ bottom(바닥). take a breath = 숨을 쉬다 → 수면으로 올라가야 함

questions.passage: A short while later, I saw that the wound had healed. To my amazement, a little arm started to grow back, and she started to become active again. I started to compare my life to life in the unforgiving sea. I thought of what was ①<u>valuable</u> in life. I began to spend ②<u>more</u> time with my family and friends. He became just as ③<u>interested</u> in her as I was. As the octopus's arm became more ④<u>dysfunctional</u>, I felt things in my life were improving too.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 문어의 팔이 더 기능적이(functional) 되면서. dysfunctional(기능 장애의)은 functional(기능적인)의 반의어이므로 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ dysfunctional(기능 장애의) → functional(기능적인)이 원문. 팔이 회복되어 기능이 좋아지는 문맥에 dysfunctional은 부적절
❌ ① valuable(가치 있는): 원문 그대로
❌ ② more(더 많은): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ interested(흥미를 가진): 원문 그대로
det.tip: functional(기능적인) ↔ dysfunctional(기능 장애의). 접두사 dys- = 이상, 장애. improving과 연결 → 긍정적 방향

questions.passage: I saw a fish peacefully swimming near a heap of shells. Suddenly, an octopus sprang from the heap and grabbed the fish. Amazed at the cleverness of the octopus, I swam a little closer, but it disappeared. In fact, it had lifted a piece of seaweed, wrapped it around itself, and was staring at me out of a little gap. What an __________ creature!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 정말 비범한(extraordinary) 생물이구나!
det.analysis:
✅ ③ extraordinary(비범한): 해조류로 위장하는 놀라운 행동에 대한 감탄. 원문 일치
❌ ① ordinary(평범한): extraordinary의 반의어. 감탄 문맥에 부적합
❌ ② boring(지루한): 호기심을 유발하는 문맥에 부적합
❌ ④ dangerous(위험한): 감탄의 맥락이 아님
det.tip: What an extraordinary creature! = 감탄문. 해조류 위장이라는 놀라운 행동 → extraordinary

questions.passage: I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing wildness she represented. I built a relationship with her and witnessed her life up to the final moments. I saw her from a __________ that I could not have had without this experience. She was smart, sensitive, and strong, often going through rough and tough days just like humans do.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 경험 없이는 가질 수 없었을 관점(perspective)에서 그녀를 보았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② perspective(관점): 경험을 통해 얻은 새로운 시각. 원문 일치
❌ ① distance(거리): 관계의 친밀함과 맞지 않음
❌ ③ laboratory(실험실): 야생 관찰이지 실험이 아님
❌ ④ photograph(사진): 사진이 아닌 관점의 문맥
det.tip: perspective = 관점, 시각. see ~ from a perspective = ~의 관점에서 보다

questions.passage: The shark had taken a bite of one of her arms and was waiting for her. I wanted to save my friend, but in this environment, I could only observe. She managed to get deeper into the crack, but she was bleeding. After a while, the shark lost interest, and the octopus used the opportunity to get back to her den, without one of her arms.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 화자가 직접 상어를 쫓아내 문어를 구했다.
문어는 팔 하나를 잃고 굴로 돌아갔다.

det.korean: 문어는 팔 하나 없이(without one of her arms) 굴로 돌아갔다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 팔 하나 잃고 돌아감: 'get back to her den, without one of her arms' 원문 일치
❌ ① 직접 구함: could only observe(관찰만 가능)
❌ ② 다치지 않음: taken a bite + bleeding(출혈)
❌ ③ 끝까지 추적: shark lost interest(관심을 잃음)
det.tip: without one of her arms = 팔 하나 없이. shark lost interest = 상어가 관심을 잃었다

questions.passage: A short while later, I saw that the wound had healed. To my amazement, a little arm started to grow back, and she started to become active again. I began to spend more time with my family and friends, and I even started to dive with my young son. He became just as interested in her as I was.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 화자의 아들도 문어에 대해 관심을 갖게 되었다.
화자는 문어가 다친 후 방문을 중단했다.

det.korean: 화자의 아들도 문어에 관심을 갖게 되었다(became just as interested).
det.analysis:
✅ ② 아들도 관심: 'He became just as interested in her as I was' 원문 일치
❌ ① 상처 안 나음: wound had healed(상처 치유됨)
❌ ③ 방문 중단: 계속 방문하며 확인함
❌ ④ 팔 안 자람: a little arm started to grow back(팔 재생)
det.tip: just as interested in ~ as I was = 나만큼 ~에 관심이 있는. 비교 구문

questions.passage: After mating, she didn't come out of her den. There would be no feeding or hunting. She was timing her final moments for the hatching of her eggs. After the eggs hatched, she died. A few months later, my son found a little octopus. We believe her story continues on.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 짝짓기 후 문어는 굴에서 나오지 않았다.
문어는 알을 낳은 후에도 먹이를 사냥했다.
화자의 아들이 나중에 작은 문어를 발견했다.

det.korean: 원문: There would be no feeding or hunting. 먹이도 사냥도 없었다. '사냥했다'는 불일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 먹이 사냥함: 원문은 'no feeding or hunting'이므로 먹이도 사냥도 하지 않았음
❌ ① 굴 안 나옴: didn't come out of her den 원문 일치
❌ ③ 부화 후 죽음: After the eggs hatched, she died 원문 일치
❌ ④ 아들이 발견: my son found a little octopus 원문 일치
det.tip: no feeding or hunting = 먹이도 사냥도 없음. 알의 부화를 위해 모든 것을 포기

questions.passage: I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing wildness she represented. I built a relationship with her and witnessed her life up to the final moments. I saw her from a perspective that I could not have had without this experience. She was smart, sensitive, and strong, often going through rough and tough days just like humans do. Eventually, she committed herself to protecting the birth of her young before she died. As a human being, I found something noble in that sacrifice.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 문어는 인간에게 위협이 되는 해양 생물이다.
야생 동물과의 접촉은 질병 전파의 위험이 있다.
자연 속 생물과의 교감을 통해 삶의 고귀한 가치를 발견할 수 있다.
해양 생태계 보존을 위해 다이빙을 자제해야 한다.

det.korean: 문어와의 관계를 통해 희생의 고귀함과 삶의 가치를 발견했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 교감→고귀한 가치: 관계 구축 + noble sacrifice + 삶의 성찰이 핵심
❌ ① 위협적 생물: 우호적 관계를 다루는 내용
❌ ② 질병 전파: 건강 문제와 무관
❌ ④ 다이빙 자제: 다이빙을 통한 긍정적 경험
det.tip: 핵심: noble sacrifice = 고귀한 희생. 문어와의 교감이 삶의 가치 발견으로 이어짐

questions.passage: I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing wildness she represented. I built a relationship with her and witnessed her life up to the final moments. She was smart, sensitive, and strong, often going through rough and tough days just like humans do. Eventually, she committed herself to protecting the birth of her young before she died. She was not simply an octopus; she was a part of this world just as I am a part of it now, and in that sense, we all have our own stories to tell.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 인간과 자연의 존재적 연결과 각 생명의 이야기

det.korean: 그녀는 이 세계의 일부이며 우리 모두 각자의 이야기가 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 존재적 연결+이야기: a part of this world + our own stories to tell. 핵심 메시지
❌ ② 생물학적 특성: 과학 정보가 아닌 철학적 성찰
❌ ③ 보호 구역: 환경정책과 무관
❌ ④ 촬영 기법: 기술적 내용 아님
det.tip: a part of this world = 이 세계의 일부. 인간도 문어도 같은 세계의 구성원

questions.passage: An octopus's average life is about a year, which ends after reproducing. One day, eight months after meeting her, I found her with another octopus. <u>It was bittersweet knowing her final days were approaching even though she would bear young.</u>
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 문장이 함축하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 화자는 문어가 다른 문어와 함께 있어서 질투를 느꼈다.
화자는 문어의 죽음이 불가피하다는 사실에 분노했다.
새 생명의 탄생에 대한 기쁨과 문어의 죽음에 대한 슬픔이 공존했다.

det.korean: bittersweet = 씁쓸달콤한. 새끼를 낳지만(기쁨) 곧 죽을 것(슬픔)이라는 양가감정.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 기쁨+슬픔 공존: bittersweet = bitter(쓴) + sweet(달콤한). 번식의 기쁨과 죽음의 슬픔 동시
❌ ① 질투: bittersweet은 질투의 감정이 아님
❌ ② 번식 방해: bear young(새끼 낳기)을 긍정적으로 봄
❌ ③ 분노: bittersweet에 분노는 포함되지 않음
det.tip: bittersweet = 기쁨과 슬픔이 동시에 존재. even though = ~에도 불구하고 (양보)

questions.passage: The shark had taken a bite of one of her arms and was waiting for her. I wanted to save my friend, but in this environment, I could only observe. She managed to get deeper into the crack, but she was bleeding. After a while, the shark lost interest, and the octopus used the opportunity to get back to her den, without one of her arms. She was in serious danger because <u>her</u> arms function like the hands, legs, nose, and eyes of humans.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 her가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그녀(= 문어)의 팔이 인간의 손, 다리, 코, 눈처럼 기능한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 문어: 앞 문맥에서 the octopus = she로 지칭. her arms = 문어의 팔
❌ ① 상어: 상어의 팔이 아닌 문어의 팔
❌ ③ 사람 친구: my friend = 문어를 가리키는 표현
❌ ④ 해조류: 팔이 없음
det.tip: her = the octopus. 이 글에서 she/her는 모두 문어를 지칭 (it → she 전환 이후)

questions.passage: I began to spend more time with my family and friends, and I even started to dive with my young son. He became just as interested in her as I was. As the octopus's arm became more functional, I felt things in my life were improving too. An octopus's average life is about a year, which ends after reproducing. One day, eight months after meeting her, I found <u>her</u> with another octopus.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 her가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그녀(= 관찰해 온 문어)를 만난 지 8개월 후, 그녀(her)가 다른 문어와 함께 있는 것을 발견했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 관찰해 온 문어: 8개월간 관찰해 온 대상 = her. found her with another octopus
❌ ② 아들: He로 지칭되는 인물
❌ ③ 다른 문어: another octopus와 함께 있는 '그녀'
❌ ④ 가족: 가족은 복수
det.tip: her = 글 전체에서 관찰해 온 '그' 문어. another octopus = 짝짓기 상대 (별개)

questions.passage: Danger in the form of pyjama sharks, the area's biggest predators, came with little warning in the sea. The octopus was moving around near the edge of the seaweed forest, and I saw a shark tracking her. In an instant, she swam into a crack to escape, but the shark was faster.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"파자마 상어는 그 지역의 가장 큰 __________(이)었다."

det.korean: 그 지역의 가장 큰 포식자(predators).
det.analysis: 원문 'the area's biggest predators'에서 predators를 찾아 쓰는 문제.
det.tip: predator = 포식자. biggest predators = 최대 포식자. pyjama shark = 파자마 상어

questions.passage: She was smart, sensitive, and strong, often going through rough and tough days just like humans do. Eventually, she committed herself to protecting the birth of her young before she died. As a human being, I found something noble in that sacrifice.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"결국 그녀는 죽기 전에 새끼의 탄생을 보호하는 데 자신을 __________(했다)."

det.korean: 자신을 헌신했다(committed).
det.analysis: 원문 'committed herself to protecting'에서 committed를 찾아 쓰는 문제.
det.tip: commit oneself to = ~에 헌신하다, ~에 전념하다. committed = commit의 과거형

questions.passage: I went diving in the cold sea off the coast of the Cape, and it was among the dense seaweed forests where I met an octopus. I saw a fish peacefully swimming near a heap of shells. Suddenly, an octopus sprang from the heap and grabbed the fish. __________. I wondered what would happen if I kept watching it.
questions.stem:
(정답은 **영어**로 작성) 다음 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)

[ what / an / extraordinary / creature ]

det.korean: 정말 비범한 생물(extraordinary creature)이구나!
det.analysis: What + an + 형용사 + 명사 = 감탄문. What an extraordinary creature!
det.tip: 감탄문 어순: What + a/an + 형용사 + 명사 + (S + V)! extraordinary는 모음 시작 → an

questions.stem:
(정답은 **영어**로 작성) 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 빈칸을 채우시오.

"나는 이 경험 없이는 가질 수 없었을 관점에서 그녀를 보았다."

I saw her from a perspective that I could not have __________ without this experience.

det.korean: 이 경험 없이는 가질 수 없었을(could not have had) 관점.
det.analysis: could not have had = 가질 수 없었을 것이다 (가정법 과거완료). have 뒤에 p.p.(had) 필요.
det.tip: could not have had = 가질 수 없었을 것이다. could not have + p.p. = 과거 사실의 반대 가정

questions.stem:
(정답은 **영어**로 작성) 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 빈칸을 채우시오.

"그녀는 단순한 문어가 아니었다; 그녀는 내가 지금 그 일부인 것처럼, 이 세계의 일부였다."

She was not simply an octopus; she was a part of this world just __________ I am a part of it now.

det.korean: 내가 지금 그 일부인 것처럼 = just as I am a part of it now.
det.analysis: just as S + V = ~인 것처럼. as는 접속사로 '~처럼, ~와 같이'의 의미.
det.tip: just as = 마치 ~처럼, ~와 같이. 비교/유사의 접속사. just as A, so B = A처럼 B도
